To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the EU CT policy is a work in progress, which is still in the making, but that there are some positive signs of progress in the right direction.
, in the context of the EU CT fight, human rights protection and enhanced security are mutually reinforcing, interdependent and complementary objectives.
the EU CT policy is not yet in a position to reconcile the two imperatives of human rights protection and the security objective.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether the EU CT policy is viable or whether it is a wishful thinking.

the question whether the EU is able to strike a balance between the demands of security and the protection of human rights in its CT policy and whether this balance is reflected in the legal framework of the EU and in the content of specific instruments.
the question of whether the EU is able to provide adequate protection of human and fundamental rights while simultaneously ensuring the security of EU citizens.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the EU has made significant progress towards the fulfilment of the objectives of security and human rights protection in its CT policy.
the EU has taken important steps in the direction of a more effective CT policy.
the EU has a long road to travel in order to reconcile the human rights safeguards and security objectives of its CT policy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, despite the progress achieved in the EU legal framework, the EU CT policy still has to address the challenges posed by the simultaneous fulfilment – or, in other words, by the reconciliation – of the security and human rights objectives.

the EU has a long way to go in order to ensure that the CT measures it adopts are not disproportionate to the objectives they pursue, that they are not applied in an arbitrary way and that they respect fundamental rights and freedoms.

, in the EU, we are still in the midst of the pendulum’s swing towards the strengthening of the EU’s security policy, but that the EU’s human rights safeguards are also gradually being strengthened, although the process is slow and uneven.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the context of the CT field, the EU is still in a learning process and, in order to achieve its stated objectives, it needs to be more transparent and accountable in its decision-making.
, in the context of the CT policy, the EU has not yet managed to achieve an appropriate balance between the two imperatives of security and human rights.

the EU is not only a normative power but also an actor with a specific approach to the fight against terrorism and the protection of human rights, and that the pendulum model of decision-making is not applicable to the EU CT policy, which is a unique and sui generis policy.
